title: Oficina Leme counter
question: The roll assigned the gauge board. Keep it, take the bin stencil, adopt a demoted card, or re-roll.

options.label: Gauge board
options.thesis: On-hand is a needle, and the requested quantity is the mark it must not pass.
options.viewport: One large dial, the part code in the hub, a row of small dials for the queue, and the manager's lock on the bezel.
options.risk: The big dial can swallow the queue if the small dials shrink to decoration.

raised.raise: The requested quantity is drawn as the mark the needle must not pass.
Pending, approved, and refused are named plates; the needle is never the only signal.
Signal red owns the live gauge; the aluminum wall stays quiet.
The part code and the quantity sit on visible ticks.
The needle snaps to a tick and never rests between marks.
Status is a physical mark on the dial, not a color chip.

options.label: Bin stencil
options.thesis: The screen is the cage: each part is a stencil plate on a galvanized lip.
options.viewport: A wall of bin lips, the open bin huge, the code stenciled, the quantity chalked on the lip.
options.risk: Caution yellow and stencil type are where industrial screens usually land.

options.label: Tensegrity column
options.thesis: A requisition is tension between the request and the bin.
options.viewport: A floating column of rods, each requisition a cord the clerk can trace.
options.case: Workshop clerks do not read a sculpture, and the stock check disappears into the diagram.
options.kept: Every request has a visible opposing mark.
options.risk: The counter becomes a sculpture and the issue gets lost.

options.label: Cyclorama dawn
options.thesis: Sign-out, pending, and approved are phases of light.
options.viewport: A curved horizon, the requisition standing in a band of dawn.
options.case: A lighting plot hides the bin count, and color would be doing the status work alone.
options.kept: Each state keeps a spoken cue name.
options.risk: Status becomes a mood and fails the contrast check.

options.label: Civic prospectus
options.thesis: The workshop presented as a funded bureau, ribbon and seals.
options.viewport: A quiet white plate, one ribbon, the counter reduced to a seal row.
options.case: This is a brochure for a visitor, and the clerk came to issue a belt.
options.kept: One saturated instrument, everything else quiet.
options.risk: The task slides under the ribbon.

options.label: Grid specimen
options.thesis: The part code is a letterform built on a visible grid.
options.viewport: A full-bleed construction grid with the part code assembled from cells.
options.case: The poster proves an alphabet. The clerk needs the bin, not the letter.
options.kept: The grid under the code stays visible.

options.label: Arcade cabinet
options.thesis: The counter is a tile grid with scanlines and a score.
options.viewport: A 240-line playfield, parts as sprites, on-hand as a score.
options.case: A cabinet is not this shift, and a score fights a bin count.
options.kept: Marks land on ticks, never between them.
options.risk: The desk starts to look like a game.

options.label: Cutting bench
options.thesis: Requisitions hang as frames on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: One orange rail of punched frames, the stopped frame flagged, the rest hung on pins.
options.case: The rail is a clear queue, and it is the wrong room: the mechanism is the bin level, not an edit.
options.kept: State is a mark on the object, not a hue.
options.risk: The orange field becomes the product and the part code shrinks.

canonCard.label: Admin shell
canonCard.thesis: A left rail, white cards, and a blue button, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: A side nav, a table of parts, and a primary button at the top of the form.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other internal tool.
